moments.title: The River Pit Steal
moments.description: Blue carry is outnumbered near the objective. Secure the pit before red completes control, or stabilize an escape through the lower river.

mechanics.name: River Core
mechanics.description: The gold-ringed River Core is a capturable objective. Uncontested blue presence inside its ring adds one blue control point at the end of a turn; uncontested red presence does the same for red. If both teams are inside, control stalls. Four points secure it.
mechanics.roleInScenario: Securing the Core is one way to win this replay. The lower-river escape is also valid, so entering the objective ring is a strategic choice rather than a requirement.

victory.description: Secure the River core before red completes control, or hold the lower-river safe zone for two turns.
victory.defeatDescription: The blue carry was eliminated before the objective or escape route was secured.

referenceReasons: Disengage immediately while the opposing formation is still committed to the objective.
Enter the lower-river safe zone before the pursuer can close the route.
Sidestep within the safe zone so the pursuing fighter cannot reset escape progress.
The authored line has already completed; hold is retained only to keep the reference horizon explicit.
The authored line has already completed; hold is retained only to keep the reference horizon explicit.

authoring.analystRationale: The carry begins near a contested objective with one visible front-line threat, a collapsing mage, and an unseen support. The scenario teaches that securing the modeled objective is not always the strongest available outcome when the safe route is already viable.
intendedTradeoffs: Entering the pit can create objective pressure, but exposes the carry to the mage collapse and hidden support.
Retreating concedes objective tempo while preserving the carry and completing a reliable lower-river escape.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The visible jungler is already low and allied support remains in shielding range.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Immediate damage may create a steal window, but delays the safe-route timer.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The mage closes and the unseen contact cannot be accounted for.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: The objective may be lost, but the carry avoids an unfavorable collapse.

acceptanceTests.name: immediate disengage completes the safe route

moments.title: Base Gate Reversal
moments.description: A low-health blue squad can punish an isolated carry before the tank arrives, or disengage through the base gate.

victory.description: Eliminate the isolated red carry before reinforcements stabilize, or hold inside the base gate for two turns.
victory.defeatDescription: The blue carry was eliminated before the target or escape condition was secured.

referenceReasons: Pressure the exposed carry before the red tank enters protection range.
Continue only while the target remains isolated and in attack range.
Brace as the reinforcement closes and let allied protection absorb pressure.
Take the final attack window before the reinforcement can fully protect the carry.
If the target survives, brace and reassess rather than inventing another attack.

authoring.analystRationale: The visible fight is temporarily two versus one. The scenario isolates the beginner lesson of focusing the exposed carry before the tank can enter protection range.
intendedTradeoffs: Immediate focus fire spends health and cooldowns to remove the highest-value exposed target.
Waiting reduces immediate risk but gives the opposing tank enough time to stabilize the carry.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The red carry remains isolated and inside closing distance.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: This maximizes target pressure while accepting return damage.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The red tank has already entered protection range.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Guarding reduces incoming damage but may forfeit the elimination window.

acceptanceTests.name: focus fire removes the isolated carry

moments.title: Outer Shrine Countdown
moments.description: Blue has four turns to clear a wounded jungler and establish uncontested control of the outer shrine.

mechanics.name: Outer Shrine
mechanics.description: The gold inner ring is a capturable objective. A team earns one control point after a turn with allied units inside and no opponents inside. Both teams in the ring make it contested, so neither gains progress. Blue needs two points to secure it.
mechanics.roleInScenario: The wounded red jungler begins close enough to deny control. Blue must remove or displace that defender, then keep uncontested presence inside the gold ring for two turns.

mechanics.name: Shrine Ring
mechanics.description: The larger blue-tinted ground around the Shrine marks its approach area and slows movement slightly. It does not award capture progress by itself; only the smaller gold objective ring does.
mechanics.roleInScenario: The approach ring affects how quickly units enter or leave the fight, while the inner ring shows exactly where Blue must stand to gain Shrine control.

victory.description: Clear the shrine edge and hold uncontested control for two turns.
victory.defeatDescription: Blue lost the shrine window before establishing control.

referenceReasons: Guard while the wounded defender commits to the edge of the shrine.
Dodge across the defender's approach and draw it away from uncontested control.
Move into the shrine once the defender has left the capture ring.
Complete the second uncontested control tick without extending past the objective.

authoring.analystRationale: A low-health objective defender creates a legible sequence: guard its first approach, dodge it out of the capture ring, then move into the shrine long enough to score control.
intendedTradeoffs: Contesting delays capture progress while removing the only nearby defender.
Retreating preserves health but allows uncontested red capture ticks.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The wounded jungler remains the only red unit inside the shrine ring.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: The carry accepts a short exchange to unlock later objective control.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The carry attack is cooling down and support protection is available.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: No damage is dealt this turn, but incoming damage is reduced.

acceptanceTests.name: draw defender out then capture shrine

moments.title: Brush Flank Collapse
moments.description: Blue can absorb the exposed mage's first approach, then collapse before the hidden tank reaches the fight.

victory.description: Bait the exposed mage into range and eliminate it before the red tank stabilizes the fight.
victory.defeatDescription: The mage survived until the red formation closed.

referenceReasons: Hold the brush edge so the exposed mage commits before its tank can screen.
Convert the mage's approach into focused damage while it remains isolated.
Guard during the attack cooldown and let the allied tank intercept.
Use the second damage window before the red tank can fully screen.
If the mage survives, hold formation rather than chase through the wall.

authoring.analystRationale: The mage is punishable, but chasing shortens the hidden tank's route. The authored line introduces a guarded bait before target focus.
intendedTradeoffs: Repositioning spends one damage turn to improve the engagement angle.
Immediate contest applies pressure sooner but leaves the carry in the reinforcement lane.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The tank is still hidden behind the wall and the mage has no nearby screen.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue delays its first attack to create a safer collapse angle.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The mage is already inside attack range and visibly unsupported.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue gains tempo but accepts a more direct counter-engage path.

acceptanceTests.name: guarded bait then focus eliminates mage

moments.title: Tower Lane Exit
moments.description: A low-health carry has a clear route to the allied tower while two opponents approach from outside immediate threat range.

victory.description: Reach the allied tower zone and remain unthreatened for two turns.
victory.defeatDescription: The carry was eliminated before stabilizing under the tower.

referenceReasons: Start moving before the jungler reaches attack range.
Continue the route while the slower class movement keeps the carry outside the tower ring.
Complete the route into the allied tower zone and start the stabilization timer.
Remain guarded until the escape condition completes.

authoring.analystRationale: The scenario makes disengagement timing visible: the safe route is available now, but disappears once the faster pursuer reaches the carry.
intendedTradeoffs: Retreating immediately gives up damage opportunities but starts the only reliable escape timer.
Holding or contesting may trade some health from an opponent while allowing the pursuit to close.

plausibleAlternatives.when: Both opponents remain outside immediate threat range and the tower path is open.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: The carry concedes lane pressure in exchange for survival.

plausibleAlternatives.when: A pursuer has already reached the route and an extra guarded turn is needed.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Guarding reduces one exchange but makes no progress toward the tower.

moments.title: Fogline Breakout
moments.description: Blue must route around vision-blocking terrain while a visible jungler and two uncertain contacts close from different angles.

victory.description: Break line of sight, reach the lower-left exit, and stabilize there for two turns.
victory.defeatDescription: The mage was caught before completing the fogline route.

referenceReasons: Cut behind the central brush instead of retreating through the visible jungler.
Turn toward the exit once the brush blocks the direct chase lane.
Continue the guarded route before the hidden mage can establish range.
Continue toward the expanded exit pocket at the mage class movement limit.
Enter the edge of the lower-left safe zone and start stabilizing.
Continue through the exit pocket to complete the second stabilization turn.

authoring.analystRationale: The direct safe-zone vector crosses two threat lanes. The authored route first uses brush geometry to break the visible chase before committing to the exit.
intendedTradeoffs: The brush detour costs distance but reduces how many enemies can maintain vision.
Direct retreat is faster geometrically but can keep the aggressive jungler on the same line.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The central brush is uncontested and the visible jungler is approaching from the upper side.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: The detour delays safe-zone entry but disrupts the direct pursuit.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The carry has already crossed behind the brush or the upper chase lane is closed.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Retreat gains speed and guard but follows the fixed safe-zone vector.

acceptanceTests.name: turning to fight loses the exit

moments.title: Support Anchor Line
moments.description: The carry can step back toward allied support before the enemy jungler and mage enter overlapping threat ranges.

victory.description: End the exchange with the carry inside the support line and the stronger tactical state.
victory.defeatDescription: The carry was isolated outside allied protection.

referenceReasons: Move back toward support before the two enemy threat ranges overlap.
Use guard and the refreshed support shield to absorb the first collapse.
Contest the nearest threat after the mage has spent its first attack window.
Hold the restored formation instead of chasing beyond support range.

authoring.analystRationale: This fixture encodes the participant insight that the carry should move back toward support when the jungler is nearby. It teaches ally-relative spacing before damage optimization.
intendedTradeoffs: Moving toward support gives up immediate damage but restores shielding and a safer firing line.
Stepping forward can poke the jungler sooner but enters overlapping jungle and mage pressure.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The jungler enters the lane while support remains behind the carry.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue loses one attack window to restore protective spacing.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The carry is already inside support range and expects the first enemy cooldowns.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Guarding preserves formation but does not widen the gap from the mage.

moments.title: Choke Range Discipline
moments.description: A mage must hold the edge of a narrow choke while allied tank protection separates an assassin from the red back line.

victory.description: Maintain maximum casting range through the choke and finish with the stronger tactical state.
victory.defeatDescription: The mage crossed the tank line and was collapsed on inside the choke.

referenceReasons: Shift laterally so the tank stays between the mage and assassin.
Cast at the nearest visible threat from maximum range.
Guard during cooldown while the tank continues the intercept.
Use the second range window without crossing the choke midpoint.
Hold the surviving formation through the final response.

authoring.analystRationale: The correct position is defined by a moving ally screen and two enemy ranges, not a fixed safe coordinate. The line rewards lateral spacing and cooldown discipline.
intendedTradeoffs: Lateral movement preserves the tank screen but delays the first spell.
Crossing the choke creates a shorter attack path while exposing the mage to assassin and carry ranges.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The assassin is approaching the tank's right edge and the red carry remains hidden.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: The mage maintains a safe angle but spends the turn repositioning.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The assassin is visible at maximum casting range with the tank still screening.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: The mage deals damage but starts its cooldown and may need to guard next turn.

moments.title: Cannon Wave Trade
moments.description: Blue can spend two safe attack windows to remove a low-health carry, but only if it guards while the first cooldown recovers.

mechanics.name: Cannon Wave
mechanics.description: The highlighted lane strip represents the cannon-wave trade area and slows movement slightly. It does not award capture progress or deal damage by itself.
mechanics.roleInScenario: The wave frames a short resource trade: use an available attack window, guard while the cooldown recovers, and avoid chasing beyond the controlled lane space.

victory.description: Trade two controlled attack windows for the exposed carry without chasing the tank line.
victory.defeatDescription: The target survived and converted the trade into red tempo.

referenceReasons: Spend the first available attack on the high-value exposed carry.
Guard during cooldown instead of paying health for an unavailable attack.
Use the recovered attack window to complete the favorable trade.
Stop at the wave line rather than chase the arriving tank.

authoring.analystRationale: The controlled resource is the attack cooldown and the carry's limited health. The intended line attacks only when damage is available and guards between windows.
intendedTradeoffs: Contesting on an available cooldown converts health risk into meaningful target damage.
Contesting while cooling down closes distance without damage and can donate health to the response.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The attack is available and the exposed carry remains the nearest visible target.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue accepts return damage for a high-value health trade.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The attack is cooling down or the tank is entering protection range.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Guarding deals no damage but protects the next useful attack window.

moments.title: Buff or Base Timing
moments.description: A low-health mage can leave the enemy buff and preserve its reset, or remain for a contested resource while unseen reinforcements approach.

mechanics.name: Red Buff Cache
mechanics.description: The gold-ringed cache uses objective control. A team with uncontested presence inside gains one control point each turn; both teams inside stall progress. Six points secure the cache.
mechanics.roleInScenario: The cache is the high-risk win route, not a mandatory pickup. Blue begins low on health while an unseen reinforcement approaches, so the value of contesting must be weighed against the reset.

mechanics.name: Reset Path
mechanics.description: The dashed blue safe zone records one escape point when the controlled mage ends a turn inside with no red unit within 18 map units. Leaving it or being threatened resets that progress. Two consecutive safe turns complete the reset.
mechanics.roleInScenario: This is the lower-risk alternative to fighting for the cache. Reaching and holding the path preserves the mage instead of spending health on the optional objective.

victory.description: Secure the buff only if the fight is favorable; otherwise reach the reset path and stabilize for two turns.
victory.defeatDescription: The mage lost both the contested resource and its safe reset.

referenceReasons: Treat low health and missing enemies as a reason to value the reset over the buff.
Continue through the brush before the visible jungler closes.
Continue around the reset brush at the mage class movement limit.
Enter the reset zone with guard still active.
Hold the route while unseen reinforcements remain outside threat range.
Complete stabilization instead of returning for a late resource contest.

authoring.analystRationale: The scenario treats the buff as optional and the low-health reset as the scarce strategic resource. Hidden reinforcement timing makes a mechanically available contest strategically poor.
intendedTradeoffs: Retreating concedes the local buff but preserves health, tempo, and the next map action.
Contesting can secure immediate value only if the unseen reinforcement is late.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The mage is below half health and at least one red contact is missing.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue gives up the buff to preserve the reset timing.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The red jungler is disabled or the missing mage has been confirmed elsewhere.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue can gain the buff but remains exposed until the second capture tick.

moments.title: Unseen Brush Check
moments.description: A visible mage is baiting near a vision-blocking brush while the enemy assassin is unaccounted for.

mechanics.name: Allied Lane Pocket
mechanics.description: The dashed blue pocket is a safe regroup zone. The controlled carry earns one escape point by ending a turn inside with no red unit within 18 map units. Leaving it or being threatened resets progress; two consecutive safe turns complete the regroup.
mechanics.roleInScenario: The pocket gives Blue a concrete destination when the assassin is missing. Stabilizing beside support is the intended alternative to walking into the bait brush.

victory.description: Respect the missing assassin, regroup with support, and stabilize in the allied lane pocket.
victory.defeatDescription: The carry entered the unverified brush and was collapsed on.

referenceReasons: Dodge the first visible skillshot without entering the unverified brush.
Move toward support to restore allied vision overlap.
Continue the support-side route at the marksman class movement limit.
Enter the allied lane pocket with guard active.
Hold the pocket long enough to complete the escape timer.

authoring.analystRationale: The visible mage is not the full situation. The fixture teaches beginners to treat an unaccounted assassin and blocking brush as actionable information.
intendedTradeoffs: Regrouping with support gives up a possible poke on the mage but reduces the blind flank angle.
Walking into the brush can reveal the assassin sooner, but only by exposing the carry to immediate threat range.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The assassin is missing and support vision is available behind the carry.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue concedes forward space to verify the next move safely.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The assassin has been confirmed elsewhere and the mage is isolated.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue can pressure the visible target but loses the guard from retreating.

acceptanceTests.name: dodge then support regroup avoids blind collapse

moments.title: Missing Flank Signal
moments.description: Blue sees a vulnerable carry in mid, but two red contacts are missing behind the side wall.

mechanics.name: Exit Pocket
mechanics.description: The dashed blue pocket is a safe exit zone. The controlled carry earns one escape point by ending a turn inside with no red unit within 18 map units. Leaving it or being threatened resets progress; two consecutive safe turns complete the escape.
mechanics.roleInScenario: The pocket preserves a retreat route if support-side vision does not make the visible carry safe to attack. It turns uncertainty into a clear fallback plan.

victory.description: Only commit to the visible carry after restoring support-side vision; otherwise preserve the retreat route.
victory.defeatDescription: The visible bait survived while the missing flank closed.

referenceReasons: Move into support-side vision before deciding whether the visible carry is truly isolated.
Hold through the flank reveal and keep shield coverage.
Disengage once the flank information confirms that the visible carry is bait.
Continue toward the exit as the missing jungler reaches the side wall.
Stabilize in the exit pocket rather than re-enter the bait lane.

authoring.analystRationale: A low-health visible carry invites commitment, but two missing contacts make target health an incomplete signal. The line checks the flank with allied vision before choosing damage or exit.
intendedTradeoffs: Vision-side movement delays target damage while improving information and support coverage.
Immediate focus can remove the carry faster but commits before the missing flank is resolved.

plausibleAlternatives.when: Two red contacts are missing and support can reveal the side wall safely.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue spends one turn on information rather than target damage.

plausibleAlternatives.when: The jungler appears inside flank distance or the carry gains support shielding.
plausibleAlternatives.tradeoff: Blue abandons the elimination window to preserve the controlled unit.

acceptanceTests.name: vision check then exit survives flank
